chronic joint pain in her hands and back

candidates.name: Scleroderma
support_spans: persistent hand and foot edema with new erythema
contradict_spans: negative antinuclear antibody, extractable nuclear antigen panel, and rheumatoid factor
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of persistent hand and foot edema with new erythema could be indicative of scleroderma, but the negative laboratory results make this less likely.

candidates.name: Infective endocarditis
support_spans: 4-year history of injecting heroin, buprenorphine, suboxone, and morphine without tourniquet use
contradict_spans: echocardiogram showed a normal ejection fraction
candidates.why: The patient's history of intravenous drug use increases her risk for infective endocarditis, but the normal echocardiogram results make this less likely.

candidates.why: The patient's biopsy results are consistent with erythema elevatum diutinum, a rare skin condition characterized by small-vessel ectasia and perivascular lymphocytes.
